chunks: And through this same chain of narrators — from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa, from Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ashʿari — from Abu ʿAbd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Nothing invalidates wudu except a hadath, and sleep is a hadath.'

key_terms.اَلنَّوْمُ: sleep — here explicitly classified as a hadath, a nullifier of wudu
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat and other acts of worship
key_terms.حَدَثٌ: hadath — a ritual impurity event (such as sleep, urination, or defecation) that nullifies wudu

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), does sleep break wudu?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational legal principle: wudu is nullified only by a hadath (a ritual impurity event), and sleep is explicitly and categorically declared a hadath. This ruling confines the nullifiers of wudu to defined legal causes and authoritatively resolves that sleep — regardless of duration — constitutes a nullifier requiring renewed ablution before prayer.
